beats.narration_text: I'm Jow-hway Lee. This is the pitch for my final project: Dusk Duel, a small fighting game I have been building in Godot since Assignment 2.

My final project will take Dusk Duel to a complete, playable vertical slice that runs in a web browser: one stage, one player against a CPU opponent, from the title screen to the knockout and a rematch.

Akaken walks in; the fight starts

beats.role_note: Real Movie Maker capture of an isolated copy (capture/game, dff6cba), scripted input. This is the desktop game as it is; the browser part of the sentence is a 'will'.

beats.narration_text: Much of that loop already exists. Today the game starts on a title screen, runs a full round against a CPU opponent, ends on a K.O., and offers a rematch. All of this runs on desktop now.

result screen: AKAKEN WINS, Enter: rematch

shot.label: REAL CAPTURE · scripted input · Godot 4.7.2 · rev dff6cba · Akaken's keys sent by a capture bot · Aotake = the game's own CPU

beats.role_note: Same capture: K.O. at 21.3 s, result 22.8 s, rematch 25.3 s, round 2 at 26.3 s.

beats.narration_text: What will be new is three things: a web build, a stronger CPU opponent with adjustable difficulty, and wider tests, with a test report a stranger can re-run.

beats.narration_text: My reference is The King of Fighters '97, which I played. I like its fast combat, attack timing and defence. Dusk Duel takes a smaller approach: one complete single-player match, for someone who wants a quick fight without installing a large game, finding an online opponent, or going through setup.

props.title: Smaller, On Purpose
props.status: COMPARABLE · The King of Fighters '97, played by Zhaohui · named only, no images
props.source: Source: pitch/PROJECT-BRIEF.md Revision 2 question 3, Revision 3 item 1

beats.narration_text: Here's the CPU today, in cpu controller dot G D. On line fifty, if I attack close by, it often blocks. Line fifty-three: out of kick range, it walks in. Line fifty-five: too close, it steps back. Line fifty-seven: in range, it kicks. It makes a new decision every ten ticks.

line 53 highlights: out of kick range: walk in
line 55 highlights: too close: step back
line 57 highlights: in range, cooled down: kick

beats.narration_text: And here it is in the capture. Ah-oh-tah-keh blocks Ah-kah-ken's punches, then kicks. In round two the capture stops sending keys, so Ah-oh-tah-keh walks in and kicks a standing Ah-kah-ken. Next, I want its choices to be more deliberate, not just more frequent.

beats.narration_text: I'm aiming at gameplay programmer roles. The reader is a technical lead or a recruiter. In the first sixty seconds they should open the page, press Enter, fight a round, and see the K.O. and the rematch, without reading any code.

beats.narration_text: I have measured cost before. On this laptop's Intel UHD Graphics, the hit sparks added about a hundredth of a millisecond of GPU time. I will measure desktop against the browser the same way.

beats.narration_text: What it will not do: no online play, one stage only, no character select, no saves, and no big roster.

props.title: Deliberately Out
props.imageLabel: what the project will not do

beats.narration_text: The first new piece is milestone one: a full match in a web browser. I will check it on this machine, in Microsoft Edge. The game loads, I start from the title, the CPU approaches, attacks and blocks, the effects draw, the round reaches the K.O., and a rematch plays. A recording and a test report will show it ran.

beats.narration_text: The risk is that the web build looks or runs differently from desktop: shader colour, particle blending, frame rate. So the web export comes first, not last. I will compare both in the same scene, and give any effect that fails a simpler fallback.

show.event: desktop vs empty browser frame; Risk card lights

props.title: What Could Sink It
props.imageLabel: left: real capture · right: constructed, proposed

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Shaders, particles, animation and tests are skills I already have, and each has a tagged assignment behind it. What is new to me is a smarter CPU opponent, shipping a Godot game to the web, repeatable benchmarks, and wider gameplay tests.
